body.p: This listing of claims will replace all prior versions and listings of claims in the application:

br.br:
1. (Currently Amended) A computer-implemented method of assessment of ischemia and related disorders, the method comprising:
receiving a non-invasive patient-specific anatomic model including a portion of a patient's bowel;
receiving a patient physiological state, the physiological state being a state different from a resting state;
determining a blood flow demand of the portion of the patient's bowel modeled by the non-invasive patient-specific anatomical model, based on a determined mass of the portion of the patient's bowel, amount of visceral vasculature and collateral pathway(s) supplying blood to the portion of patient's bowel modeled by the non-invasive patient- specific anatomic model, and the received physiological state of the patient;
calculating a blood flow characteristic of blood delivered to the portion of the patient's bowel using the determined blood flow demand and a value of microvascular resistance based on the received physiological state;
determining a threshold blood flow characteristic based on the non-invasive patient-specific anatomic model of the patient's bowel and a predetermined healthy or average blood flow characteristic based on a population-based measurement or estimate; and
generating and displaying (i) an assessment of blood supply adequacy defining an adequacy of blood supply to the patient's bowel, or (ii) a risk score defining a risk of disease of the patient's bowel, based on a comparison of the calculated blood flow characteristic to the received threshold blood flow characteristic.
2. (Previously Presented) The computer-implemented method of claim 1, wherein the blood flow characteristic includes one or more of blood pressure, flow rate, fractional flow reserve, or portal venous pressure.
3. (Previously Presented) The computer-implemented method of claim 1, further comprising:
determining the blood flow demand based on an allometric relationship between blood flow and the determined mass of the portion of the patient's bowel.
4. (Currently Amended) The computer-implemented method of claim 3, further including:
subdividing the non-invasive patient-specific anatomic model into one or more bowel regions;
determining an association between a vessel of the patient's vasculature and at least one bowel region of the one or more bowel regions; and
determining blood flow adequacy for one or more locations of the portion of the patient's bowel distal to the at least one bowel region, based on a determined blood flow adequacy for the at least one bowel region.
5. (Previously Presented) The computer-implemented method of claim 1, further comprising:
calculating the blood flow characteristic using a fluid simulation or using blood flow characteristics based on one or more other patients.
6. (Previously Presented) The computer-implemented method of claim 1, wherein the value of microvascular resistance comprises resistance at a vessel outlet.
7. (Currently Amended) The computer-implemented method of claim 6, further comprising:
modifying a geometry of the non-invasive patient-specific anatomic model;
determining a blood flow characteristic at a location in the non-invasive patient- specific anatomic model based on the modified non-invasive patient-specific anatomic model; and
generating an updated assessment or display of blood supply adequacy to the patient's bowel, or
generating or displaying a risk score for risk of disease to one or more regions of the patient's bowel, based on the calculated blood flow characteristic at a location in the modified non-invasive patient-specific anatomic model.
8. (Previously Presented) The computer-implemented method of claim 1, further comprising:
determining the risk score for risk of disease to one or more regions of the patient's bowel based on the assessment of blood supply adequacy to the patient's bowel, wherein the risk of disease includes risk of one or more of mesenteric ischemia, intestinal ischemia, ischemic colitis, abdominal pain, gangrene, bowel perforation, sepsis, stricture, and inflammatory conditions.
